shortDescription: STOCKS TO WATCHDefence contractor Babcock International hiked its interim dividend, continued progress on its £200m share buyback programme and reiterated full-year guidance on Thursday after reporting double-digit growth in first-half profits, earnings and cash flow. children: hiked its interim dividend, continued progress on its £200m share buyback programme and reiterated full-year guidance on Thursday after reporting double-digit growth in first-half profits, earnings and cash flow. Babcock said underlying operating profits rose 13% to £227m, while underlying earnings per share increased 15% to 32.7p. Underlying operating margins improved by 50 basis points to 8.4%, moving the group closer to its medium-term target of at least 9%, while underlying free cash flow increased to £186m. Net cash excluding leases stood at £35m, representing a £91m year-on-year improvement. Group revenues increased 5% organically to £2.7bn, driven by strong performances in its nuclear and aviation divisions.

trimmed full-year guidance on Thursday, after third-quarter sales were hit by unseasonably warm weather and the riots in France. Updating on trading, the chain said like-for-like sales in the 13 weeks ended 31 October had fallen 2.6% to £2.9bn, or by 1.1% on an organic basis. Within that, conditions improved in North America compared to the second quarter, and organic growth ticked up 0.5%. In Europe, on the other hand, like-for-like sales fell 2.7%, impacted by unseasonably warm weather at the start of autumn and civil unrest in France. As a result, JD Sports narrowed its full-year guidance and now expects pre-tax profits before adjusting items to come in between £700m and £750m, down from previous expectations for between £700m and £800m.

Wall Street stocks delivered a mixed performance on Wednesday, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average tumbling more than 500 points as Nvidia reversed early gains and minutes from the Federal Reserve's latest meeting pointed to further interest rate increases.
